[Filing a Claim]
There are two routes. Which one is available depends on whether the hospital is
in the Aurora network, not on the plan you hold.

meta.heading: Filing a Claim

text:
[Filing a Claim > Route 1 — Cashless (network hospitals only)]
1. Present your Aurora health card and a government photo ID at the hospital
   insurance desk.
2. The hospital submits a pre-authorisation request to Aurora.
3. For a **planned** admission, submit the request at least **72 hours** before
   admission. Aurora responds within **4 working hours** of receiving a complete
   request.

meta.heading: Filing a Claim > Route 1 — Cashless (network hospitals only)

text:
[Filing a Claim > Route 1 — Cashless (network hospitals only)]
4. For an **emergency** admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within
   **24 hours** of admission. Aurora responds within **1 hour** for emergencies.
5. Aurora settles the approved amount directly with the hospital. You pay only
   the non-payable items, any co-payment, and anything above the sum insured.

meta.heading: Filing a Claim > Route 1 — Cashless (network hospitals only)

text:
[Filing a Claim > Route 1 — Cashless (network hospitals only)]
A pre-authorisation approval is an estimate, not a final settlement. The final
amount is decided on discharge against the actual bill.

meta.heading: Filing a Claim > Route 1 — Cashless (network hospitals only)

text:
[Filing a Claim > Route 2 — Reimbursement (any hospital)]
Use this at non-network hospitals, or where cashless was denied.

meta.heading: Filing a Claim > Route 2 — Reimbursement (any hospital)

text:
[Filing a Claim > Route 2 — Reimbursement (any hospital)]
1. Notify Aurora within **48 hours** of an emergency admission, or **72 hours
   before** a planned admission. Notification is by app, portal, or the 24×7
   helpline. Failure to notify does not by itself void the claim but must be
   explained.
2. Pay the hospital yourself and collect the complete document set.

meta.heading: Filing a Claim > Route 2 — Reimbursement (any hospital)

text:
[Filing a Claim > Route 2 — Reimbursement (any hospital)]
3. Submit the claim within **30 days of discharge**.
4. Submit post-hospitalisation bills within **15 days** of the end of the
   post-hospitalisation period applicable to your plan.

meta.heading: Filing a Claim > Route 2 — Reimbursement (any hospital)

[Filing a Claim > Settlement timelines]
Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within **15 working
days** of receiving the last required document. If Aurora raises a query, the
clock restarts when you supply the queried document. Where Aurora exceeds the
regulatory settlement timeline, interest is payable at the bank rate plus 2%.

An insured on Silver with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured has a room-rent limit of
2%, i.e. ₹10,000 per day. They occupy a room at ₹15,000 per day for 4 days.
The eligibility ratio is 10,000 ÷ 15,000 = 0.667.

A family floater is a single shared pool. If a ₹10,00,000 Silver floater covers

[Glossary]
**AYUSH** — Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy.

**Cashless facility** — Settlement made by Aurora directly to a network hospital,
so that the insured does not pay and then claim.

**Co-payment** — A fixed percentage of every admissible claim that the insured
bears. Distinct from a deductible, which is an absolute amount.

meta.heading: Glossary

text:
[Glossary]
**Cumulative bonus / No-claim bonus** — An increase in sum insured granted for a
claim-free year, at no additional premium.

**Day-care procedure** — A procedure that requires less than 24 hours of
hospitalisation because of technological advance, and is therefore payable
despite the general 24-hour admission requirement. Out-patient treatment is not
a day-care procedure.

meta.heading: Glossary

text:
[Glossary]
**Deductible** — An absolute amount the insured bears before cover begins. Aurora's
indemnity plans do not carry a deductible; its top-up products do.

**Domiciliary hospitalisation** — Treatment at home for a condition that would
normally require hospitalisation, where the patient could not be moved or a bed
was unavailable.

meta.heading: Glossary

text:
[Glossary]
**Free-look period** — The window in which a new policy can be returned for a
refund.

**Grace period** — The window after the due date in which a renewal premium may
be paid without losing continuity. Cover does not operate during it.

**Indemnity** — Reimbursement of actual expenses incurred, up to a limit, as
opposed to a fixed payout on the occurrence of an event.

meta.heading: Glossary

text:
[Glossary]
**Migration** — Moving between products of the same insurer with waiting-period
credit.

**Network hospital** — A hospital with which Aurora has an agreement to provide
cashless treatment.

**Portability** — Moving to a different insurer with waiting-period credit.

meta.heading: Glossary

text:
[Glossary]
**Pre-existing disease (PED)** — A condition diagnosed, treated, or symptomatic
and known to the insured in the 48 months before policy commencement.

**Pre- and post-hospitalisation** — Related medical expenses incurred in a
defined window before admission and after discharge, payable as part of the same
claim.

meta.heading: Glossary

text:
[Glossary]
**Proportionate deduction** — Reduction of associated hospital charges in the
ratio of the eligible room rent to the actual room rent.

**Restoration** — Automatic reinstatement of an exhausted sum insured within the
same policy year.

**Sub-limit** — A cap on a specific head of expense that sits below the overall
sum insured.

meta.heading: Glossary

text:
[Glossary]
**Sum insured (SI)** — The maximum Aurora will pay in a policy year, before any
no-claim bonus or restoration.

**Third Party Administrator (TPA)** — An intermediary that processes claims on
an insurer's behalf. Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA.

**UIN** — Unique Identification Number allotted to an insurance product by the
regulator.

meta.heading: Glossary

[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Renewal]
All Aurora indemnity plans are lifelong renewable. Aurora may not decline
renewal on grounds of the insured's age, claims history, or adverse change in
health. Renewal may be declined only for established fraud, misrepresentation,
or non-disclosure of a material fact.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Renewal

text:
[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Renewal]
Premium is not guaranteed. Aurora may revise premium rates with the approval of
the regulator, but only for an entire product cohort, never for an individual
policyholder on the basis of their claims.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Renewal

text:
[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Grace period]
The grace period is **30 days** from the renewal due date for annual policies
and **15 days** for policies paid in instalments.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Grace period

text:
[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Grace period]
Cover is **not** in force during the grace period. A claim for an admission that
occurs inside the grace period, before the renewal premium is received, is not
payable. What the grace period preserves is *continuity*: renew inside it and
your waiting periods and no-claim bonus carry forward unbroken.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Grace period

text:
[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Grace period]
Renew after the grace period expires and the policy is treated as fresh. All
waiting periods restart, accumulated no-claim bonus is lost, and fresh
underwriting applies.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Grace period

text:
[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Portability]
You may port an existing health policy from another Indian insurer to Aurora at
your renewal date, keeping the waiting periods you have already served.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Portability

text:
[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Portability]
- Apply at least **45 days** and no more than **60 days** before your existing
  policy's renewal date.
- Aurora must accept or decline within **15 days** of receiving the complete
  portability application and the previous insurer's data.
- If Aurora does not respond within 15 days, the application is deemed accepted.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Portability

text:
[Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Portability]
- Credit for waiting periods served is granted **only up to the sum insured of
  the previous policy**, including its accrued no-claim bonus. Any increase in
  sum insured is subject to fresh waiting periods on the incremental amount.
- Portability is not available mid-term, only at renewal.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Portability

text:

Migration is moving between Aurora's own products — for example Silver to Gold.
The rules are the same as portability with respect to waiting-period credit, but
no 45-day notice is required; migration can be requested at any renewal.

meta.heading: Renewal, Grace Period, and Portability > Migration

particular kind of claim becomes payable. Waiting periods run from the date of
first policy commencement, not from each renewal, provided coverage has been
continuous without a break of more than 30 days.

[Aurora Top-Up and Super Top-Up Plans]

text:
[Aurora Top-Up and Super Top-Up Plans > The difference between top-up and super top-up]
- **Top-up**: the deductible applies to **each single claim**. A ₹5L deductible
  with two ₹4L claims pays nothing.
- **Super top-up**: the deductible applies to the **aggregate of all claims in
  the policy year**. The same two ₹4L claims exceed ₹5L in aggregate, so ₹3L is
  payable.

partial images are the most common cause of a claim query, and a query
restarts the settlement clock.
